title: Best Air Purifiers UK
short: HEPA air purifiers compared by CADR, room size, noise and who they suit, including allergy and baby-safe picks.
intro: An air purifier can help with dust, pet dander, pollen and general indoor air quality, but the right size and features depend on the room. This guide compares purifiers from Expert Reviews' testing, from compact bedroom units to models built for large living rooms.

products.name: Big+Quiet Formaldehyde

products.key_spec: 100m2 room size, HEPA and carbon filters
products.summary: Expert Reviews' top pick overall. Its HEPA and carbon filter combination removes a wide range of pollutants including formaldehyde, and it doubles as a cooling fan.

guide.q: What size air purifier do I need?
guide.a: Check the manufacturer's maximum room size rating and choose a purifier rated at or above the size of your room. A purifier that is too small for the room will run constantly on a high, noisy setting to keep up.
CADR (Clean Air Delivery Rate) measures how quickly a purifier cleans the air in a room, usually in cubic metres per hour. A higher CADR generally means faster air cleaning for a given room size.

guide.q: Do air purifiers actually help with allergies?
guide.a: A true HEPA (H13-grade) filter captures 99.95% of airborne particles down to 0.1 microns, which Allergy UK recommends as the minimum standard for allergy sufferers. Purifiers can reduce dust and pollen in the air, though they will not remove allergens already on surfaces.

guide.q: Where should I put an air purifier?
guide.a: Place it in the room you spend the most time in, away from walls and furniture so air can circulate freely, and avoid tucking it into a corner where airflow is restricted.
